title: Naval 专题 · 读他之前：四个折扣
title_en: Naval Series · Before You Read Him: Four Discounts

questions.question: Naval 说「在一千个平行宇宙里，你要在九百九十九个里都变得富有」。按「位置」这一折扣，这句话对一个普通创业者的问题在哪？
options: 问题在于他低估了勤奋的作用，普通人只要更努力就能弥补运气的差距
这句话本身没有问题，只要判断力足够好，任何人都能在大多数宇宙里致富
问题在于平行宇宙只是比喻，现实中无法验证，所以这句话没有意义
投资人能靠组合里一两笔赢家抹平失败，创业者只有一张票、一条时间线
questions.explanation: 天使投资的回报几乎全来自一两笔，手里一百张票九十张作废也没关系；他自己也讲过遍历性：一百个人的平均不等于一个人重复一百次。拿组合视角给只有一张票的人开「不靠运气」的承诺，正是位置带来的落差。
questions.question_en: Naval says "in 1,000 parallel universes, you want to be wealthy in 999 of them." Under the "position" discount, what's the problem with this for an ordinary founder?
options_en: The problem is that he underrates hard work; ordinary people can make up for luck by trying harder
Nothing is wrong with it; with good enough judgment, anyone can get rich in most universes
The problem is that parallel universes are just a metaphor that can't be tested, so the line is meaningless
An investor's one or two winners cover a portfolio of losses; a founder holds one ticket on one timeline
questions.explanation_en: Angel returns come almost entirely from one or two deals, so ninety dead tickets out of a hundred don't matter. He himself has explained ergodicity: what holds on average across a hundred people doesn't hold for one person repeating a hundred times. Offering a "without luck" promise from a portfolio seat to someone holding one ticket is the gap that position creates.

questions.question: Naval 提出：教人致富又靠这个赚钱的人，钱最好是在别处赚的。按「动机」这一折扣，他自己的情况应如何看？
options: 他过了这条检验，钱确实是在别处赚的，所以他的建议没有利益冲突，不必再打动机折扣
动机折扣不适用于他，因为他的财富主要来自运气而非任何主动布局
他没过这条检验，因为他的播客靠广告和付费课程盈利
他过了这条检验，但大部分身家压在未上市创业公司，劝人投身创业与他的仓位同向
questions.explanation: 按他自己的标准他是过关的：播客不放广告、不卖东西，钱在别处赚。但动机不在课程而在仓位：他大部分身家在未上市公司，劝科技从业者把钱「加倍」投回科技业，搭档也直说免不了替自己的持仓说话。
questions.question_en: Naval says anyone teaching how to get rich while profiting from it should have made their money elsewhere. Under the "motive" discount, how should his own case be seen?
options_en: He passes the test, his money really was made elsewhere, so his advice has no conflict of interest and needs no motive discount
The motive discount doesn't apply, since his wealth came mainly from luck rather than any deliberate positioning
He fails that test, because his podcast makes money from ads and paid courses
He passes the test, but most of his wealth sits in private startups, so urging people into startups matches his positions
questions.explanation_en: By his own standard he passes: the podcast has no ads and sells nothing, and his money was made elsewhere. But the motive lies in his positions, not courses: most of his net worth is in private startups, he urged tech workers to "double down" on tech, and his co-host admitted they probably talk their book.

questions.question: Naval 说二十年前他认定聪明又勤奋的人，现在几乎无一例外都成功了。按节目页的核查，这个说法最主要的漏洞是？
options: 说法完全属实，研究证实有能力的人几乎必然成功
聪明和勤奋其实与创业成功毫无关系，成功完全取决于运气
他的判断力只适用于 2009 年以前的硅谷，那之后创业的市场环境已经完全不同了
没有分母：他记得的只是仍在视野里的人；连成功过的创业者再上市也只有约三成
questions.explanation: Gompers 等人的数据显示能力确实会延续，但上一家成功上市的人，下一家上市的概率也只有 30%。他的样本是自己记得、仍在视野里的人；聪明和成功都会让人更容易留在视野里，这正是伯克森悖论式的筛选。说「毫无关系」则走向了另一个极端。
questions.question_en: Naval says nearly everyone he judged smart and hardworking twenty years ago has since succeeded. Per the page's fact-check, what is the main flaw in this claim?
options_en: The claim is entirely accurate; research confirms capable people almost always succeed
Intelligence and hard work actually have nothing to do with startup success, which depends entirely on luck
His judgment only applied to Silicon Valley before 2009, and the startup market has been completely different since then
No denominator: he recalls only people still in view; even proven founders take their next company public only about 30% of the time
questions.explanation_en: Gompers et al. show skill does persist, but founders whose last company went public have only a 30% chance with the next. His sample is people he remembers who remain in view, and both intelligence and success make people likelier to stay in view, a Berkson-style selection. Saying skill is irrelevant goes to the opposite extreme.
